Interface BodyElements<T>

Type Parameters:
T - The type of an element
All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
All Known Implementing Classes:
ReleasingBodyElements
Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface BodyElements<T> extends AutoCloseable
The elements of a body, one at a time, like a cursor: pulled by whoever reads them.

Reading a request body

AsyncRequestBody.elements(Class) reads a JSON array or a JSON stream as elements, decoded as they are asked for. Nothing is read ahead of the caller: the next element is received and decoded when next() is called, or when the stage the forEach(Function) consumer returned for the previous element completes.

request.elements(Person.class)
    .forEach(person -> people.saveAsync(person))
    .thenApply(done -> HttpResponse.accepted());

Writing a response body

Returned as the body of a response, the elements are pulled by the server as the connection takes the bytes of the previous ones, and written with the message body writer of the content type of the response, exactly like the elements of a Publisher body, but without Reactive Streams. With a JSON content type they are written as a JSON array, with text/event-stream as server-sent events (an element may be an Event), and otherwise one after the other; a ByteBody element is written as its bytes arrive. Elements read from a request body, or by the HTTP client, can be returned as they are:

routes.GET("/books", (request, pathVariables) -> {
    Cursor<Book> cursor = books.open();
    return HttpResponse.ok(BodyElements.of(cursor::nextAsync, cursor::close))
        .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_TYPE);
});
routes.POST("/echo").body().handleAsync((request, pathVariables, body) ->
    CompletableFuture.completedStage(HttpResponse.ok(body.elements(Person.class))));

The response is sent once the first element (or the end) is available: if the first next() fails, the failure is answered like a failure of the route; a later failure ends the response abruptly. next() is called again only after the stage it returned completed, and only while the bytes the connection has not taken yet stay below a high-water mark (micronaut.server.responses.stream.high-water-mark), so a slow client pauses the elements. It is called on a thread of the server, usually an event loop: it must not block, and should return a stage that another thread completes if producing the element takes time. close() is called once when the response ends: after the end, after a failure, when the client disconnects, when the body is not written (a HEAD request), and when a filter replaces the response or its body. A filter that replaces them with other elements hands them over: the new elements are closed instead, and close these if they wrap them.

The rules

One operation at a time: an operation started while another one is in progress throws an IllegalStateException, at once, instead of returning a stage. The end of the body and closing are different: at the end of the body, next() completes with an empty optional and forEach(Function) completes normally, while closing during an operation completes that operation with a CancellationException, and an operation started after closing throws an IllegalStateException. An element that the elements of of(Supplier) produce after they were closed is not delivered: it is closed if it is AutoCloseable, e.g. a CloseableByteBody. The elements of a request body are closed when the method that read them completed, see AsyncRequestBody, unless they are the body of its response; closing them discards the rest of the body.

The instances of the framework, and those of of(Supplier), enforce the rules; a lambda does not, and is only ever called by one caller at a time when the server writes it. The stages of the instances of the framework complete on a thread chosen by the server, usually an I/O thread: a consumer must not block.

      Read the next element.
      Returns:
      Completes with the element, with an empty optional at the end of the body, or exceptionally when reading or decoding the body fails
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if another operation is in progress, or the elements were closed

    • forEach

      default CompletionStage<Void> forEach(Function<? super T, ? extends CompletionStage<?>> consumer)
      Consume the remaining elements in order. The next element is read when the stage returned for the previous one completes. Elements that are available at once are consumed in a loop, so many of them do not deepen the stack. A failure of a consumer does not close the elements.
      Parameters:
      consumer - Consumes an element, completing when it is done with it
      Returns:
      Completes when every remaining element was consumed, or exceptionally when reading the body or a consumer fails
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if another operation is in progress, or the elements were closed

    • closeAsync

      default CompletionStage<Void> closeAsync()
      Close the elements, e.g. discard the rest of the body. An operation that has not completed ends with a CancellationException. For the instances of the framework, closing again returns the same stage.
      Returns:
      Completes when the elements were closed, or exceptionally if closing failed

    • close

      default void close()
      Close like closeAsync(), without waiting for it. Does nothing by default: elements that hold resources, e.g. a database cursor, release them here.
